source_cards.title: Automatic Music Mixing using a Generative Model of Effect Embeddings (MEGAMI)
source_cards.bounded_summary: Automatic mixing is modeled as a conditional distribution of plausible professional decisions rather than one deterministic target. The system generates coordinated per-track effect embeddings, augments them with track-level dynamics and stereo descriptors, and evaluates generative outputs with distributional distances plus a listening test.
limitations: The main listening test used 12 volunteers, only seven songs, and wide song-dependent confidence intervals.
The evaluated model assumes time-invariant track-level embeddings and no master-bus effects.
Some training and evaluation data are internal; results do not establish production readiness for live rock.
Study-reported KAD and listening scores are not universal acceptance thresholds.

source_cards.title: MEGAMI official implementation
source_cards.bounded_summary: Public research implementation, inference scripts and checkpoints are available. The repository documents 44.1 kHz dry-track input and a noncommercial CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.
limitations: No local inference or audio evaluation was run in this update.

source_cards.title: Beyond Dry References: Learning Relative Audio Effects Representations via Contrastive Distance Learning (RelFx)
source_cards.bounded_summary: RelFx learns the direction and distance of an effect transformation between ordered audio pairs without requiring a truly dry reference. Same-section cross-segment sampling reduced content shortcuts; retrieval accuracy alone did not reliably track style-transfer performance.
limitations: Overall transformations are modeled, but source-specific effects inside a full mixture are not separated.
Unseen chain order and real production chains remain future work.
The principal style-transfer score is an embedding-guided/MRSTFT protocol; no broad rock-production listening study was reported.
Training used licensed internal audio plus MoisesDB and substantial GPU compute.

source_cards.title: StemFX: Learning Mixing Style Representations via Autoregressive FX Chain Prediction on Source-Separated Stems
source_cards.bounded_summary: StemFX predicts variable-length, ordered, per-stem effect chains rather than forcing every target through a universal fixed chain. In the paper's real-mix test, fixed-chain methods often introduced distortion or modulation absent from the target; blind listeners preferred the sparse structure-selecting approach over the tested fixed-chain baselines.
limitations: The system is limited to four separated stems and effect types present in training.
Pseudo-stems inherit separator artifacts, whose propagation was not quantified.
Random training chains may not capture genre-dependent engineering practice.
The listening study used 20 music-production participants and study-specific material; reported scores are not universal targets.

source_cards.title: StemFX official implementation
source_cards.bounded_summary: MIT-licensed code, model interface, evaluation scripts and paper checkpoint links are available. The API can accept a mixture or four pre-separated stems and returns an inspectable per-stem chain.
limitations: No code, model, weights or audio were executed in this update.
The paper workflow expects 44.1 kHz and GPU-oriented research tooling.

source_cards.title: MultiAFx official implementation
source_cards.bounded_summary: MIT-licensed Python wrapper exposing a serializable chain format and 85 effects from seven libraries, with parameterized min/mid/max tests described in the repository.
limitations: Parameter ranges are research/tool defaults, not musical presets.
Compatibility, numerical equivalence and real-time safety for Automixer were not tested.

knowledge_cards.title: Automatic mixing is one-to-many
knowledge_cards.claim: A single set of dry tracks can support multiple valid professional mixes; deterministic regression can collapse toward an over-conservative average.

knowledge_cards.title: Relative effect change can be learned without a truly dry reference
knowledge_cards.claim: For reference matching, modeling the ordered transformation from current sound to target may be more robust than treating the target as an absolute effect state.

knowledge_cards.title: Match musical section when learning or measuring change
knowledge_cards.claim: Adjacent, non-overlapping clips from the same section reduced content shortcuts in RelFx; verse-to-chorus comparisons can confound production change with arrangement change.

knowledge_cards.title: Select processor topology before fine parameter search
knowledge_cards.claim: A universal chain with all processors nominally bypassable can still create artifacts; choosing which effects and their order is a distinct problem from estimating parameter values.

knowledge_cards.title: Stem-aware representations help but inherit separation errors
knowledge_cards.claim: Per-stem input improved the study's representation results, but pseudo-stem artifacts were not quantified and must be treated as a confound.

knowledge_cards.title: One objective metric is not a sufficient acceptance gate
knowledge_cards.claim: In RelFx ablations, retrieval accuracy sometimes improved while style-transfer loss worsened; automatic mixing evaluation needs independent metrics and level-matched listening.

candidate_rules.summary: Generate and rank several bounded mix candidates instead of assuming one deterministic optimum.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Offline automatic mixing or creative reference matching.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Sample several coordinated candidate control sets inside existing safety bounds; retain explicit controls and human override.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Source identity, section hierarchy, transients, mono compatibility, editability.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Level-match candidates; compare independent spectral/dynamic/spatial descriptors; run blind listening against current baseline.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Reject candidate generation if variants collapse to the same mix, become unstable, or only improve one metric.

candidate_rules.summary: Compare current-to-target change, not only absolute target descriptors.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Reference matching when the input is already processed or no truly dry reference exists.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Estimate a directional delta per comparable section and stem; apply a bounded fraction of that delta before remeasurement.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Musical content, phase, groove, timbral identity, existing useful processing.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Use same-section clips, loudness-match, verify whether the target distance closes on more than one independent descriptor, then listen blind.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Cancel if the delta reverses on a repeat measurement, depends strongly on section content, or increases artifacts.

candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Any reference or style comparison across songs or mix versions.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Compare chorus with chorus and verse with verse; use adjacent non-overlapping windows when possible; aggregate only after section-level checks.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Arrangement contrast, transient shape, role hierarchy.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Repeat with several windows inside each section and check sign consistency of the inferred changes.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Do not generalize a change when its direction flips across comparable windows or when sections are structurally dissimilar.

candidate_rules.summary: Choose a sparse processor topology and order before optimizing exact parameters.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Offline chain inference, reference transfer, or automatic correction proposals.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: First decide bypass/effect/order candidates; then optimize parameters only for the retained processors.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Clean transients, absence of unintended distortion/modulation, latency budget, interpretability.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: A/B topology-first, universal fixed-chain, and current manual baseline with equal loudness; inspect every active processor and null/bypass behavior.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Remove any processor whose activation does not create a repeatable perceptual or target-distance improvement.

candidate_rules.summary: Gate stem-based reference matching on separation quality.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Using separated commercial references or pseudo-stems for analysis.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Run the same separator on candidate and reference, track artifact confidence per stem, and down-weight bands/segments dominated by leakage or separation residue.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Cymbal detail, guitar texture, vocal sibilance, phase, instrument identity.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: On a legal true-multitrack benchmark, compare clean-stem deltas with pseudo-stem deltas; require agreement before promotion.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Cancel or fall back to mixture-level analysis when pseudo-stem and clean-stem directions disagree materially.

candidate_rules.summary: Do not promote a reference-matching rule from retrieval or spectral loss alone.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Evaluation of learned effect representations or automatic mixes.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Use at least one signal metric, one perceptual/embedding metric not used for optimization, and level-matched blind listening.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Pre-register success and cancellation criteria; keep optimizer metric separate from final acceptance gates.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Reject if metric gains do not survive listening or create protected-quality regressions.

experiments.title: Relative vs absolute stem-reference matching
experiments.material: One legal four-stem rock multitrack plus one separated reference; later repeat on Premiera only locally.
experiments.success: Directional method wins preference and reduces at least two independent distances without protected regressions.

experiments.title: Topology-first vs universal fixed chain
experiments.success: Sparse chain matches or beats target similarity while activating fewer processors and causing fewer artifacts.

experiments.title: One deterministic mix vs four bounded candidates
experiments.material: One chorus and one verse from a legal rock multitrack.
experiments.success: At least one variant clearly beats the deterministic baseline and candidate diversity is musically meaningful.

experiments.title: Separator robustness gate
experiments.success: Define confidence thresholds where pseudo-stem recommendations remain directionally consistent with true stems.
